title: Graph Domain
public_summary: A graph is the single-thread concurrency domain for related updates; causal influence can still cross graphs through explicit delayed boundaries.

public_sections.heading: Use It
body: Keep tightly related updates inside one graph when they need to settle together. When work crosses a graph, process, worker, or runtime boundary, model that boundary explicitly instead of pretending it is the same immediate update.
bullets: One graph serializes its own propagation.
Cross-graph influence returns through a wire bridge or package-owned adapter.
Graph boundaries explain concurrency, not every possible causal relationship.

title: Wave
public_summary: A wave is the ordered update unit that lets dirty notifications, values, and settling behavior stay explainable.

public_sections.heading: Use It
body: Think of an update as one coherent movement through declared edges. The shared docs describe the behavior; package docs own the exact APIs that create or observe it.
bullets: One message array is one wave.
Dirty state reaches joins before changed values settle.
Downstream reducers should see coherent inputs, not half-old mixes.

title: Boundary
public_summary: Async work, host callbacks, worker pools, and remote runtimes belong at explicit boundaries that re-enter the graph with visible facts.

public_sections.heading: Use It
body: Keep ordinary graph propagation synchronous and inspectable. Put files, network calls, background workers, and cross-runtime transport behind sources, pools, adapters, or bridges that publish explicit graph-visible results.
bullets: Do not hide timers or callbacks inside reductions.
Use package-owned adapters for environment-specific IO.
Keep package API details delegated to language-local docs.
